questions.note: Height, stance width and shoulder span match the reference (shoulder-to-shoulder about 0.38 of figure height in both). The head reads too broad and boxy, with a tall spiky crest adding height; upper arms read heavier than the lean reference. Leg proportions follow the declared real thigh lengths.

Stance, feet placement and the carbine's line match well (stock-to-muzzle slope about 1.5 in both, by eye in the onion). The outline breaks at the right pauldron, which stands up and out past the drawn shoulder, at the spiky hair crest, and at the low boots, which shorten the ankle silhouette.

Every listed item is present and roughly where drawn: gaiter, carrier with three mag pouches, antenna, pauldrons, forearm guards, gloves, belt, right drop-leg panel, left hip pouches, knee pads, boots. Wrong in kind or size: right pauldron mounted as a flat board, knee pads flat boxes, boots low-cut and sneaker-like instead of a mid-height combat boot.

Order of layers is right and the belt sits under the carrier (turnaround). But the trouser hems stop above the boot collar leaving a dark sock gap, the right pauldron stands off the deltoid, the left elbow sleeve balloons outward, the knee pads sit proud with only one visible strap, and the left hand rests on the handguard without closing.

Sleeves read as smooth inflated neoprene, making the arms bulky while the kit reads light: carrier and pouches flat and clean, pauldrons pale grey plastic, boots thin-soled. The reference's worn olive-khaki carrier and dark weathered armour carry more weight; skin is orange and waxy.

Carbine line and height are right, and the right hand plausibly holds the pistol grip with the trigger finger indexed along the receiver. The left hand lies flat on top of the handguard with straight fingers, neither cupping it from below as drawn nor clamping it: it would not control the muzzle. Side views show the gun carried out at arm's length.

defects.what: Left hand lies palm-down on top of the handguard with straight, splayed fingers that never wrap it; no thumb opposes, so the hand is resting on the gun, not holding it.
defects.fix: Cup the handguard from below as drawn: palm under the rail, fingers curled over the top, thumb along the near side, knuckles flexed about 60 to 90 degrees.

defects.what: Right pauldron is a flat board hanging from the shoulder strap, standing off the deltoid and rising above the shoulder line; real shoulder armour is domed to follow the deltoid and sits on it.
defects.fix: Curve the plate around the deltoid cap, seat it on the sleeve, and hang it from the carrier shoulder strap so its top sits at the acromion, not above it.

defects.what: Trouser hem ends above the boot collar, leaving a dark band of sock or ankle; real trousers either break over the boot top or are bloused into it.
defects.fix: Lengthen the hem so it rests on the boot upper with a break and stacked folds, as the reference shows.

defects.what: Boots read as low-cut trainers: shaft barely above the ankle, thin sole, long pointed toe with no bumper; the reference and a Zephyr-class mid boot have a shaft about 150 mm high, a chunky lugged sole and a rounded rubber toe cap.
defects.fix: Raise the shaft to mid-boot height, thicken the midsole and lugs, round and bulk the toe with a rubber rand.

defects.what: Left sleeve balloons into a large rounded bulge at the elbow point; a bent sleeve stretches over the olecranon and gathers in the crook, it does not inflate outward.
defects.fix: Pull the sleeve taut over the elbow point and bunch the slack into the inner crook.

defects.what: Skin is a saturated orange, uniform and waxy, with no redness variation at nose, cheeks and ears and no paler stubble zone; the reference skin is a desaturated, weathered tan.
defects.fix: Lower saturation, add regional colour zones (redder nose and ears, bluish beard shadow) and specular breakup.

defects.what: Brows sit low on the upper lids in a scowl over a flat, slab forehead with no frontal eminences or temple hollows; the jaw reads very wide and square, making the head boxy.
defects.fix: Raise the brows to sit on the orbital rim, model the frontal bossing and temporal fossa, narrow the gonial angles.

defects.what: Hair is a spiky upright crest over clean shaved sides, reading as a mohawk; the reference has a short textured crop, top swept up and back, sides short but haired.
defects.fix: Keep a few millimetres of hair on the sides tapering to the ears and lay the top longer and swept back.

defects.what: Carrier and pouches are a flat, clean grey-olive; the reference carrier is olive-khaki Cordura with heavy edge wear, dirt and fading, and its colour shifts warmer than the render.
defects.fix: Warm the base toward olive-khaki, add abrasion on edges and pouch lids, dust in recesses and fading on the top surfaces.

defects.what: Pauldrons and forearm guards are pale, clean grey reading as plastic; the reference armour is dark grey-olive, scuffed to bright metal-like edges.
defects.fix: Darken the base value markedly, keep wear to edges and raised areas.

defects.what: Knee pads are flat-faced boxes standing proud of the trouser, with only one visible strap; AirFlex-class pads are curved shells that wrap the patella and sit in a knee pocket or under two straps.
defects.fix: Curve the cap around the knee, seat it into the trouser knee, and show the upper and lower straps.

defects.what: Mag pouches are wide, pudgy blocks butted together; real triple M4 pouches are narrow (about 75 mm each) and taller, with flaps or bungee retention and visible spacing on the PALS.
defects.fix: Narrow each pouch to one STANAG width plus wall, raise its height, add the flap or bungee.

defects.what: Two thin wire-like hooks dangle under the drop-leg panel with nothing to attach to.
defects.fix: Remove them or make them the panel's lower leg-strap buckle ends.

ranked: [D1] The left hand does not hold the carbine: it lies flat on the handguard with straight fingers. Any shooter would see the support hand is not controlling the muzzle.
[D6] Skin is orange and waxy, which reads as CG before anything else in the frame; the reference skin is a desaturated, weathered tan.
[D10] Pauldrons and forearm guards are pale clean grey plastic; the reference armour is dark and worn, so the arms jump out of the value structure.
[D9] The carrier is a flat clean grey-olive; the reference is worn olive-khaki with dirt and edge abrasion. The kit reads unissued.
[D2] The right pauldron is a flat board standing off the shoulder and rising above it, breaking the shoulder silhouette; real plates are domed and seated on the deltoid.
[D4] The boots are low trainers with thin soles and pointed toes; a combat boot of this class has a mid shaft, chunky lugged sole and a rubber toe cap.
[D3] A dark sock gap shows between trouser hem and boot collar; trousers break over the boot or blouse into it, never stop short.
[D7] The face scowls under low brows on a flat forehead with a very wide square jaw; the head reads boxy and heavier than the reference man.
[D8] The hair is a spiky crest over shaved sides, a mohawk, rather than the reference's short textured crop with haired sides.
Sleeves are smooth inflated tubes: the arms read bodybuilder-thick while the reference is lean with armour giving the bulk.
[D5] The left sleeve balloons at the elbow point instead of stretching over it and gathering in the crook.
[D11] Knee pads are flat boxes sitting proud of the leg with one strap; real pads curve around the knee.
In the side views the carbine is carried at arm's length well in front of the carrier; the reference low ready keeps it closer to the body.
Gloves read as smooth rubber with no knuckle protection or seams; Mechanix M-Pact class gloves have moulded knuckle guards visible at this size.
[D12] The front mag pouches are wide pudgy blocks rather than narrow, taller flapped M4 pouches.
Trouser upper legs read close to tights around the crotch while the lower legs are wide straight tubes; Crye G3 class cut is roomier above and tapers below.
[D13] Two stray wire hooks hang under the right drop-leg panel.
